title: Pancake Sorting
description:
Given an array of integers `arr` that is a permutation of `[1, 2, ..., arr.length]`, sort `arr` by performing a series of **pancake flips**.

In one pancake flip you do the following steps:
- Choose an integer `k` where `1 <= k <= arr.length`.
- Reverse the sub-array `arr[0...k-1]` (0-indexed).

Return an array of the `k`-values corresponding to a sequence of pancake flips that sort `arr` in ascending order. Any valid answer that sorts the array within `10 * arr.length` flips will be judged as correct. The judge simulates your flip sequence and validates that `arr` ends up sorted within the flip budget (`true`).
constraints: All integers in arr are unique (arr is a permutation of [1, 2, ..., arr.length]).
hints: Think like Selection Sort: place the largest unsorted element into its final position at the end of the unsorted prefix, one element at a time.
To move value x from index idx to its target position (x - 1), first flip the prefix of length (idx + 1) to bring x to index 0, then flip the prefix of length x to move x to index (x - 1).
Each element needs at most 2 flips, so the total number of flips is at most 2 * (n - 1), well under the 10 * n limit.

examples.explanation: The array [1, 2, 3] is already sorted, so an empty list [] of flips is valid.

inputs.name: arr
inputs.description: Permutation of integers 1..n to sort using prefix reversals
